# `Q-5-52` — Invalid `resource-discovery` Value

> `resource-discovery` must be `true` or `false`. Any other value
> stops the document from rendering, so that a typo cannot publish
> linked files the author meant to keep out.

## What this means

Quarto copies the local files that a page's markdown links point at
into the output directory, so that a link like `[Data](data.csv)`
works on the rendered site (see
[Linked files are copied](../../guides/projects/paths.qmd#linked-files-are-copied)).
`resource-discovery` turns that on (`true`, the default) or off
(`false`):

```yaml
---
title: Internal notes
resource-discovery: flase   # Q-5-52: a typo, not `false`
---
```

Any value that is not a YAML boolean is rejected, wherever it is set:
a page's front matter, a directory's `_metadata.yml`, `_quarto.yml`,
a `format:` block, `-M resource-discovery:…` on the command line, or a
Lua filter. Quoted values are strings, not booleans, so `"false"` and
`"no"` are rejected too.

This is an error rather than a warning because of what the setting
protects. Someone who writes `resource-discovery: false` usually wants
some linked files to stay off the published site. If Quarto warned
and carried on, a render in a publishing pipeline that doesn't stop on
warnings would publish exactly those files. Instead, the document is
not rendered and none of the files it links to are copied. The other
documents in the project render normally.

## How to fix it

Write the value as an unquoted boolean:

```yaml
resource-discovery: false
```

Or remove the key to keep the default, which copies linked files.

## Difference from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 always copies linked files and has no setting to turn this
off. `resource-discovery` is new in Quarto 2.
